facts.statement: Montanazhdarcho is a genus of azhdarchoid pterosaur from the Late Cretaceous period found in what is now Montana, United States.
facts.quote: Montanazhdarcho is a genus of azhdarchoid pterosaur from the Late Cretaceous period (Campanian stage) of what is now the state of Montana, United States.

facts.statement: The holotype specimen MOR 691 was found by Robert W. Harmon in Glacier County, Montana, in sandstone of the Upper Two Medicine Formation dating to about 74 million years ago.
facts.quote: The holotype specimen, MOR 691 (Museum of the Rockies), was found by Robert W. Harmon in Glacier County, in the territory of the Blackfoot, in sandstone of the Upper Two Medicine Formation, a layer about 74 million years old.

facts.statement: The genus was formally named in 1995 by the same researchers and fully described in 2002.
facts.quote: It was then named formally in 1995 by the same researchers, and was fully described in 2002.

facts.statement: Montanazhdarcho was a relatively small pterosaur with a wingspan reaching 2.5 meters.
facts.quote: Montanazhdarcho was a relatively small pterosaur, reaching 2.5 m in wingspan.

facts.statement: The jaws of Montanazhdarcho were edentulous, meaning they lacked teeth.
facts.quote: The jaws were edentulous, i.e. they lacked teeth.

facts.statement: In 2018, Nicholas Longrich and colleagues recovered Montanazhdarcho within the Azhdarchidae, placing it in the basalmost position.
facts.quote: In 2018, Nicholas Longrich and colleagues had recovered Montanazhdarcho within the Azhdarchidae again, though placed in the basalmost position.

facts.statement: Montanazhdarcho lived during the Campanian stage, between 83.6 and 72.2 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Campanian to Campanian (83.6 to 72.2 million years ago)
